solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Machiavellian as a physiotherapist?

definitions.meaning: scheming and controlling other people by cunning
a physiotherapist works by manipulating muscles and joints with the hands

explanation.surface: A question about whether a physio is a ruthless schemer.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a schemer who works on people, and a therapist who works muscles by hand.

clue.text: The Queen Mother's embraced pretentious ceremony

indicators.note: the mother word wraps its arms round the royal letters

parts.note: mummy is a child's word for mother
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: The Queen Mother has been part of some grand, showy ritual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Queen Mother' looks like one royal person, but splits into two separate pieces, with ''s embraced' meaning 'is held inside'.
explanation.definitionFit: Mummery is hollow, showy ritual, from the masked performers of old folk plays.

clue.text: Cool, though without ice?

definitions.meaning: a spirit served with no ice or mixer is ordered this way

explanation.surface: A drink that is chilled, yet with no ice in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for great, and the barroom word for a spirit poured undiluted.

clue.text: Unit overly into design

indicators.note: the word for overly goes into the word for design

parts.note: a plan is a design
too means overly, as in too much

explanation.surface: An army unit far too absorbed in some project.
explanation.definitionFit: A platoon is a military unit, a subdivision of a company.

clue.text: Toboggan packed with funny cases

indicators.note: the sled is stuffed with the joke, which goes inside it

parts.note: a luge is a small racing toboggan
a funny, as a noun, is a joke, a gag

explanation.surface: A sled loaded up with amusing suitcases.
explanation.definitionFit: Luggage means suitcases and bags taken on a journey.

clue.text: Unlikely description of a giraffe?

definitions.meaning: as in a ... story, one hard to believe
a giraffe is notably high, the tallest animal

explanation.surface: A doubt about whether some word really suits a giraffe.
explanation.definitionFit: A far-fetched tale is called this, and the word for great height also suits a giraffe.

clue.text: Identification device injected into rodent showing current potential

indicators.note: the tag goes inside the rodent, as a microchip would

parts.note: a vole is a small rodent
a tag identifies something

explanation.surface: A microchip tag is implanted in a small animal, showing its current potential.
explanation.definitionFit: Electrical potential difference, the push behind an electric current, measured in volts.

clue.text: The angler's choice halved, curiously one's hooked

indicators.note: curiously suggests something odd, so the letters come out in a strange new order
only the first half of choice is used

explanation.surface: An angler's chosen fish, cut in two, is oddly caught on the hook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'halved' keeps CHO of choice. 'hooked' suggests a fish but describes an item hung by its hook.
explanation.definitionFit: A coat hanger has a hook at the top to hang on a rail, so it is a hooked item.

clue.text: My word is no bond — get rent out!

indicators.note: out suggests being wrong or not in place, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A landlord refuses a deposit and demands the rent be extracted.
explanation.definitionFit: A British exclamation of surprise, named after a flamboyant newspaper heir; same as gosh.

clue.text: Priest screening sinful, sexy dance

indicators.note: a screen hides something behind it, so the priest's word goes round the other piece

parts.note: a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist priest
sinful means bad

explanation.surface: A clergyman hides a racy dance from view.
explanation.definitionFit: The Brazilian partner dance became famous in 1989 for its close, hip-swaying moves.

clue.text: Vessel almost entirely filled with iodine for scientist

indicators.note: the shortened ship has the element symbol put into its middle
nearly all of the ship's name is kept, losing only its final letter

parts.note: a galleon is an old sailing ship
I is the chemical symbol for iodine

explanation.surface: A ship's hold is packed with a chemical, all for the sake of some scientist.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian astronomer and physicist who championed the Copernican view of the solar system.

clue.text: Youth finds place for driving van, finally

parts.note: in golf you drive off from the tee

indicators.note: only the closing letter of van is taken

explanation.surface: A young person locates somewhere to drive a van at last.
explanation.definitionFit: A teenager is a youth, aged thirteen to nineteen.

clue.text: Something black in a seam round back of collar, a shade of pink

indicators.note: the coal goes round, enclosing the other letter

parts.note: coal is black and is mined from seams

indicators.note: the final letter of collar is taken

explanation.surface: A sooty mark in a seam near the back of a pink collar.
explanation.definitionFit: Coral is a pinkish-orange colour, named after the sea creature's skeleton.

clue.text: For example, a straight worker

definitions.meaning: in poker a straight is one kind of set of cards dealt to a player
a hired labourer, as on a farm or ship

explanation.surface: An honest worker, for example.
explanation.definitionFit: Poker deals cards in sets, of which a straight is one; a farm or deck labourer is also called this.

clue.text: Feature of a score rising and falling

definitions.note: a half note, one of the note values written in a musical score

indicators.note: in a down entry it reads the same upwards as downwards

parts.note: a half note, one of the note values written in a musical score

explanation.surface: A musical score has a feature that goes up and down.
explanation.definitionFit: A minim is a half note, one of the notes written in a musical score.

clue.text: Quality cuppa dope takes before midday

indicators.note: the fool's letters go first, ahead of the time abbreviation

parts.note: a dope is a fool, an ass
AM means before noon

explanation.surface: A fine cup of tea is drunk by some idiot before lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quality cuppa' is a fair definition because this is a premium tea; 'takes before' sets the fool ahead of the time of day.
explanation.definitionFit: Assam is a strong black tea from north-east India.

clue.text: Blissful, yes, with nail getting hammered?

indicators.note: hammered things are beaten out of shape, so the letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone happily says yes as a nail is driven in, or as they get drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting hammered' suggests drunkenness, but it is the anagram signal for YES and NAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to Elysium, the paradise of Greek myth, and so heavenly or blissful.

clue.text: Steep cracks then fashionable for sculptor

indicators.note: something that cracks breaks apart, so the letters of steep are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: in means fashionable

explanation.surface: A steep slope breaks apart, then becomes trendy for a sculptor.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Jacob Epstein was a leading twentieth-century sculptor working in Britain.

clue.text: Deer carrying piano is a musician

indicators.note: the deer word holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: a hart is a male deer
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

explanation.surface: A deer lugging a piano turns out to be a performer.
explanation.definitionFit: A player of the harp is one kind of musician.

clue.text: Turn over or below a complete circuit in a game

definitions.text: a complete circuit in a game

indicators.note: turn over means flip it, so the word or is read backwards

parts.note: under means below

explanation.surface: Flip it or go beneath to finish a full lap in some game.
explanation.definitionFit: In rounders, a bat-and-ball game, a full run round all the bases scores one of these.

clue.text: Feeling dehydrated, a bunch of fives catching southpaw's head

indicators.note: the number catches the letter and holds it

parts.note: six fives make thirty; a bunch of fives is also slang for a fist

indicators.note: only the first letter of southpaw's is taken

explanation.surface: A boxer is parched after landing a fist on a left-hander's head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bunch of fives' is British slang for a fist, which fits the boxing picture, but here means a sum of fives: thirty.
explanation.definitionFit: Thirsty means wanting a drink, which is how a dehydrated person feels.

clue.text: Bumps felt by Liberal after a beating

indicators.note: a beaten thing is battered into a different shape, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician is left with bruises after an assault.
explanation.definitionFit: The tactile writing system for blind readers uses raised dots felt with the fingertips.

clue.text: Flower — that's made with flour!

definitions.meaning: something that blooms, a flowering plant
a long crusty white loaf, a British bread

explanation.surface: A sound-alike joke about flowers and flour.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant that blooms is one; a British crusty loaf baked from flour has the same name.

clue.text: Ladies and gentlemen, a cathedral city, more or less

parts.note: the ladies and the gents are public toilets, loos
Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, England

explanation.surface: An announcer addresses the crowd in a cathedral city, roughly speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ladies and gentlemen' sounds like an audience being addressed but means two public toilets.
explanation.definitionFit: Loosely means approximately, not exactly.

clue.text: Britain behind 193 states backing northern capital

indicators.note: Britain's letters come behind, after the other piece
backing means moving backwards, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: the United Nations has 193 member states
UK is the United Kingdom

explanation.surface: Britain lags behind the world's nations in supporting a northern capital.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital city of Greenland, far in the north.

clue.text: Antigonus somewhat cross

indicators.note: only part of the name is used, the letters sitting inside it

explanation.surface: An ancient king called Antigonus was a little angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like an adjective meaning angry, but it is a noun: a hybrid animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A hybrid of a male tiger and a lioness is one kind of animal cross.

clue.text: Mint, one eaten by someone serving porridge

indicators.note: the convict swallows the letter, holding it inside

parts.note: porridge is British slang for a prison sentence, so a convict serves it; CON is short for convict
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A sprig of mint is eaten by someone dishing up oatmeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mint' is a verb here: to make money by stamping metal. 'porridge' suggests breakfast but is British slang for time in jail.
explanation.definitionFit: To mint is to stamp out money, which is what the verb meaning to stamp a token of metal also says.

clue.text: One side set out

definitions.meaning: the port or sinister side, as opposed to right

explanation.surface: One team took its position, or someone set off on a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: The side opposite to right, and the past tense of leave, meaning departed.

clue.text: Censor film about princess

indicators.note: the film's letters go round the princess

parts.note: E.T. is the Spielberg film about an alien
Di was Diana, Princess of Wales

explanation.surface: A censor cuts a film about a princess.
explanation.definitionFit: To edit is to cut or revise material, as a censor does.

clue.text: Constant, heading off straight?

indicators.note: the first letter, the head, is removed

parts.note: a straight road is bendless, having no bends

explanation.surface: A question about whether going straight ahead without stopping is constant.
explanation.definitionFit: Something constant goes on without ceasing, with no stop in sight.

clue.text: US states including Illinois — location of East and South?

definitions.meaning: the central northern region of America taking in Illinois, Ohio and others
the letters E and S sit in the middle of the compass word WEST

explanation.surface: A geography question about where Illinois sits, and about where east and south lie.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is cryptic: E and S stand at the centre of W-E-S-T.
explanation.definitionFit: The region of central northern America that includes Illinois; also the middle of the word for the opposite of east.

clue.text: Appearing twice, quite over-decorated

indicators.note: the word for quite is written out two times in a row

parts.note: pretty means quite, as in pretty good

explanation.surface: Something shows up twice and looks rather too ornate.
explanation.definitionFit: The doubled form means fussily ornamented, prettified to excess.
